sources.title: Service quality
facts: The index lists current complaint, compensation, ADR and market-report records.
It identifies service-quality material by publication and update date.
limits: An index is lineage evidence rather than proof of an individual service outcome.
Listed records have different vintages and scopes.

sources.title: Broadband complaints fall to record low
sources.geo: United Kingdom major telecoms and pay-TV providers
facts: The release covers January to March 2026.
It reports fixed-broadband complaints at six per 100,000 customers in Q1 2026.
limits: Complaints rates are provider-level aggregates.
Low complaint volume does not prove address-level service quality.

sources.title: Report: Complaints about broadband, landline, mobile and pay-TV services
facts: Ofcom publishes complaints per 100,000 customers by service and provider.
The page was updated with Q1 2026 trends on 23 July 2026.
limits: The dataset covers providers meeting publication thresholds.
Complaint rates are not a direct coverage or orderability measure.

sources.title: ADR schemes' performance
facts: Ofcom publishes quarterly KPIs for CISAS and Communications Ombudsman.
The page includes Q2 2026 performance measures.
limits: Scheme KPIs do not decide the merits of an individual complaint.
ADR performance is separate from network availability.

sources.title: Making a complaint and using alternative dispute resolution (ADR) schemes
sources.geo: United Kingdom residential, small-business and qualifying not-for-profit users
facts: Unresolved complaints can be taken to an ADR scheme for free.
For complaints raised under the current rule, access is available after six weeks or a deadlock letter.
limits: Eligibility depends on the complaint and customer category.
Guidance does not verify the facts of a particular dispute.

sources.title: Automatic compensation: What you need to know
sources.geo: United Kingdom broadband and landline customers of participating providers
facts: Participating providers pay compensation for specified service failures without a customer request.
The page lists providers participating in the scheme.
limits: Only participating providers and qualifying events are covered.
Compensation eligibility does not establish general network quality.

sources.title: Quicker complaints resolution for telecoms customers, under new Ofcom rules
sources.geo: United Kingdom residential and small-business telecoms customers
facts: Ofcom decided to reduce the ADR access threshold from eight weeks to six weeks.
The change took effect for complaints raised from 8 April 2026.
limits: The article announces a rule change rather than resolving individual complaints.
Provider complaint handling remains case-specific.

sources.title: Statement: Review of ADR in the telecoms sector
facts: The statement confirms the six-week ADR access rule.
It re-approves Communications Ombudsman and CISAS as telecoms ADR schemes.
limits: A final regulatory statement is not an individual adjudication.
Supporting PDF internals were not used.

sources.title: Quicker complaints resolution and more money in your pocket when things go wrong
facts: The six-week ADR access rule commenced on 8 April 2026.
The page also notes inflation-linked increases under automatic compensation.
limits: The update summarises protections and does not calculate a customer's award.
Compensation remains subject to scheme conditions.

sources.title: Codes of practice
sources.kind: complaints, compensation and broadband-speed code index
sources.geo: United Kingdom communications providers and customers
facts: The page identifies complaint-handling requirements and voluntary broadband-speed codes.
It lists current provider signatories to relevant voluntary schemes.
limits: An index does not replace the code text.
Provider participation and scope must be checked for the relevant service.
